title: Don't count environment stops as failed attempts in the scope guard
summary: The scope guard (crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs) currently turns every non-landed, non-rejected closed job into a Failed attempt that counts toward T1 retries, T2 planning rounds, T3 cost and T5 time. Change it so an attempt that ended on an environment cause (low disk, usage limit, interrupted process) is excluded from the attempt and round signals, and so a retry that resumes a kept candidate is judged against the cost of its remaining stages only. Audience: the operator whose line was paused. Job 20261028-034820-v3rf is the paused line, not a job to redo: its five planning-critique findings (replay.md refused by the records check, test override placement, no skip switch, Records::load question) concern the replay feature and are not touched by this guard fix. The line is not edited, only unblocked.

defaults_applied.how: The change is Rust in athena-core.
New unit tests are required, and cargo test and clippy -D warnings must pass.
The new rule is enforced in code by the guard's signal functions, with tests.
The fix changes how the guard classifies attempts, not just this one paused line.
The criteria run the tests and check pause and no-pause results.
The check is that a complete attempt stopped on the environment no longer pauses the line.
The change is one focused edit to the guard plus a changelog entry.
Doc comments explain the new rule and any estimate.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Job 20261028-034820-v3rf's findings belong to the replay feature; this change only makes the guard stop counting its environment-stopped attempt, so the findings need no fix here and its own retry is out of scope.

An environment stop is identified from the job's recorded outcome (state and reason text, e.g. low disk, usage limit, interruption) and the existing attempt_of mapping; no new record fields are added to athena-data.
An environment-stopped attempt is excluded from T1 attempt count, T2 planning round and plan growth, T4 rejections and T5 minutes; a failed verification (Rejected) still counts.
For a retry resuming a kept candidate, T3 compares spend against the p90 forecast scaled to the stages not yet done, and spend already made on the kept stages is not counted against it.
Stage cost shares are fixed constants in scope_guard.rs, labelled as estimates.
Thresholds and athena.toml are unchanged, so no governance file changes.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs builds a line whose earlier attempt ended on low disk and shows evaluate_before_attempt gives no T1/T2/T5 pause or flag from it, while the same line with a Rejected verification does. Run: cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard.

A unit test in scope_guard.rs shows a retry that resumes a kept candidate (planning, build and checks done) is judged against the cost of its remaining stages: spend that would pause as a fresh job does not pause, and the same spend on a non-resuming retry does. Run: cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard.

The existing scope_guard tests (t4_pause_via_go_and_ask, retry_refuses_paused_line, t3_pause_from_reading_forecast and the rest) still pass, so real rejections and cost overruns still pause lines. Run: cargo test.
cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings are clean.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry naming the scope guard change: environment-ended attempts are not counted, and resumed retries are forecast on remaining stages.
Each new constant or rule in scope_guard.rs has a doc comment stating its basis or marking it an estimate, and the diff touches only crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs and CHANGELOG.md.

out_of_scope: Changing the guard thresholds or the T4 same-criterion rule
Implementing the replay feature of job 20261028-034820-v3rf or retrying that job
Changing the disk check or how outcomes are recorded in athena-data
Unpausing or editing existing pause records
departures: Slightly lower pass odds than the reference: it is a gate change, and environment stops are identified from outcome reason text, which may be unstructured.
urgent_reason: It cuts wasted time: it stops the guard from pausing a line whose attempt was complete and stopped only on low disk, which forces redo-work retries.
hard_reason: It changes the scope guard, a gate that pauses and holds other jobs' work, so a mistake can wrongly pause or fail to pause lines.
